definitions.explanation: The arrangement of words in a sentence according to the grammatical rules of a language. A key concept in linguistics and language learning.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{語順|ごじゅん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{英語|えいご}→英語：02274_eigo⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{違|ちが}う→違う：01957_chigau⟧。
examples.english: Japanese word order is different from English.

examples.japanese: {語順|ごじゅん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{間違|まちが}える→間違える：01109_machigaeru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{意味|いみ}→意味：01155_imi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{変|か}わる→変わる：00714_kawaru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: If you get the word order wrong, the meaning can change.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{主語|しゅご}→主語：00377_shugo⟧・⟦{目的語|もくてきご}→目的語：20479_mokutekigo⟧・⟦{動詞|どうし}→動詞：03472_doushi⟧⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧{語順|ごじゅん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{基本|きほん}→基本：00226_kihon⟧だ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{助詞|じょし}→助詞：03351_joshi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で⟦{比較的|ひかくてき}→比較的：06172_hikakuteki⟧⟦{自由|じゆう}→自由：01148_jiyuu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{並|なら}び{替|か}えられる。
examples.english: Japanese has a basic subject-object-verb word order, but because it uses particles, words can be rearranged relatively freely.

notes:
Compound of ⟦{語|ご}→〜語：09841_go⟧ (word) + ⟦{順|じゅん}→順：03342_jun⟧ (order). Frequently encountered in language textbooks and linguistic discussions.

Japanese is classified as an SOV (subject-object-verb) language, contrasting with English SVO order. However, Japanese {語順|ごじゅん} is relatively flexible because grammatical relationships are marked by particles rather than position.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {語順|ごじゅん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{違|ちが}う→違う：01957_chigau⟧ (word order is different)
- {語順|ごじゅん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{変|か}える→変える：01089_kaeru⟧ (to change word order)
- ⟦{基本|きほん}→基本：00226_kihon⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{語順|ごじゅん} (basic word order)
- ⟦{自由|じゆう}→自由：01148_jiyuu⟧な{語順|ごじゅん} (flexible word order)
